name: Mir Space Station
tagline: For fifteen years, crews called this modular station home. Its final voyage was a carefully planned return through Earth’s atmosphere.
imageAlt: Illustrated archive portrait of Mir Space Station
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Provide a long-duration orbital research laboratory assembled from modules launched over time.
beats.achieved: Mir hosted international crews, supported long-duration human spaceflight research and helped develop operational experience later used on the International Space Station.
beats.ending: After 15 years in orbit, Mir was deliberately guided into Earth’s atmosphere on March 23, 2001. Most of the station burned up, with surviving debris falling into a designated remote area of the South Pacific.
beats.now: Mir is no longer in orbit. Its controlled deorbit ended a major chapter in human spaceflight.
beats.learned: Long-duration station operations taught engineers and astronauts how to maintain complex systems, conduct research and live in space for extended periods.
